subject: Tier transition + temporary price lock mitigation plan
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyroot.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: RevOps <revops@skyroot.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal negotiation: tier transition & temporary price lock request

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the productive renewing call earlier. As discussed, we're moving a subset of workloads to a new internal tier while our ML infra migration finishes. That migration slipped, and our projected production rollout will be delayed ~60–75 days.

Two asks from our side:
- Short-term price lock for current committed unit price for up to 90 days while we complete migration.
- A modest commit bump for Q1 to cover the onboarding burst; we propose +20% for three months with true-up afterwards.

I've attached our Q3 usage CSV to show the recent burst pattern. If Redwood can offer a 90-day price lock + a one-time credit to offset migration costs, we can confirm a multi-quarter renewal today.

Can you outline what internal approvals you need and a proposed amendment timeline?

Best,
Jane
Revenue Operations
SkyRoot Analytics
Attachments: SkyRoot_MonthlyUsage_Q3.csv (csv)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyroot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: tier transition & temporary price lock request

Hi Jane — appreciate the context and the usage file. Quick response with a pragmatic path that should be workable from our side: 

Proposal (high level):
- 90-day temporary price lock: hold committed per-unit rate for up to 90 days from the renewal effective date.
- Migration credit: one-time credit equal to 10% of the next quarter's committed spend (applied as invoice credit).
- Phased commit bump: +20% committed capacity for 3 months then 1-month true-up to reconcile actuals.
- MAP: 3-week turnaround on an amendment from signature-ready draft to countersigned SLA/commit.

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm the 20% uplift figure and whether the credit should be amortized or applied immediately.
2) Legal to accept our standard amendment language (I can send Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf).
3) If agreed, we'll route to Finance and Sales Ops for a quick credit approval (should be OK but needs Ben's sign-off).

I'll loop in Ben and Monica for approvals and will attach the draft amendment and MAP link.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd like to accelerate.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAP

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: tier transition & temporary price lock request

Ava / Monica — quick internal:
- Finance is OK with a one-time credit up to 10% of next-quarter committed spend for strategic accounts, provided Sales Ops confirms the MAP and there's an explicit true-up.
- We prefer invoice credit applied immediately rather than amortized — simpler for both parties.
- Need the final amendment, then I can sign the credit approval form.

Monica: please block 15 mins for legal/finance handoff this afternoon.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyroot.com>

Ava — thanks, that plan works for us.

Confirmations:
- We accept the 20% committed uplift for three months with a one-month true-up.
- One-time credit of 10% of next-quarter committed spend applied immediately as invoice credit is acceptable.
- 90-day price lock is acceptable as specified.

Please send the updated amendment (Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf with the committed numbers filled in) and the MAP link. Once we have the countersigned amendment, we'll process the purchase order and signature.

Onwards — appreciate the fast turnaround.
